subject: Payor identity + invoice path for marketplace activation
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@clearsky.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Marketplace activation — next steps for PO / payor setup

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the walkthrough on Monday. We're ready to move forward with the AWS Marketplace listing but procurement at Clearsky has a couple of gating asks before we can accept purchase orders: 

- Confirm the 'bill-to' / payor entity Redwood expects on invoices (doing entity validation on our side)
- A standard PO flow (will we get a numeric PO from Redwood or via marketplace billing?)
- Wiring instructions and remit-to for invoices

I've attached the vendor side forms we typically send to marketplace partners so you can see what our finance team needs. Can you share Redwood's vendor intake template and any preferred fields for PO/Invoice? Also copying procure@clearsky.ai so they see the thread.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Finance Operations
Clearsky AI
Attachments: clearsky_vendor_profile.pdf (stub), clearsky_procurement_requirements.docx (stub)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@clearsky.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace activation — next steps for PO / payor setup

Hi Elena — great to hear you're ready. Quick checklist to unblock marketplace activation from our side: 

1) Payor identity: we support either the listing owner (Redwood Inference) billing or direct invoicing to the customer (Clearsky AI). For direct invoicing we need: legal payor name, billing address, taxpayer ID (W-9 / W-8 as applicable), and preferred remit-to method.

2) PO flow: our standard is to accept a numeric PO from the buyer (Clearsky) and attach it to our invoice. For AWS Marketplace transactions sometimes the marketplace replaces the PO with a marketplace invoice — if you prefer the buyer-issued PO route please confirm and we'll mark the account for buyer-PO reconciliation.

3) Wiring / bank info: I'll share our vendor_intake_template (attached) — please fill the bank_wiring_form.xlsx and return it with your tax doc.

4) Timing: once we have the signed tax doc + bank form + confirmed payor entity, our finance team can approve the payor mapping; typical SLAs are 2 business days for mapping, 3–5 for PO acceptance into billing.

I'm attaching the Redwood vendor intake template and the bank wiring spreadsheet. Lauren, can you confirm whether we should request a DocuSign for the payor attestation for Clearsky?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Revenue Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: vendor_intake_template.pdf (stub), bank_wiring_form.xlsx (stub)

From: Elena Morales <elena@clearsky.ai>

Cc: procure@clearsky.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace activation — next steps for PO / payor setup

Thanks Neha — attaching our signed W-9 and a filled vendor profile. A few clarifications from procurement: 

- Our procurement team will keep issuing POs (numeric) — they want the PO field on your invoices populated with their PO number before payment.
- For Marketplace purchases (if billed through AWS), will Redwood accept the AWS invoice as the primary invoice for tax and audit? Or do you still require our buyer-issued PO?
- Remit: we prefer Redwood to invoice Clearsky directly (bill-to = Clearsky AI) rather than marketplace billing where possible.

Attaching: clearsky_signed_w9.pdf, clearsky_vendor_profile_filled.docx

Elena
